analysis:
This batch contains only documentation and changelog changes. The new changelog file is changelog.d/watchdog-kickstart-acknowledgement.md, lines 1-3. docs/developer/test.md head lines 318-335 add a Watchdog Launch Acknowledgement test section. docs/provider/installation.md changes the date stamp at head line 3 and adds head lines 217-224.

The documented behavior: if launchctl kickstart reports a missing service (exit 3 or 113) after a successful loaded check, kickstartIfLoaded returns noLongerLoaded. In that case the watchdog must restore the exact prior crash-loop guard bytes, invoke no trip callback and leave a stopped or uninstalled job unloaded.

The relevant threat is T-043 (TB-003): watchdog rollback authority is the same replaceable provider binary. The crash-loop guard and predecessor rollback relate to availability and downgrade behavior.

No Swift source for LaunchAgent.swift, WatchdogRecoveryService.swift or LaunchAgentLifecycleTests.swift was supplied. The claims that the rollback restores only the guard staged for the attempt, preserves a pre-existing guard, and does not suppress legitimate crash-loop rollback or predecessor rollback (T-043) are therefore unverified. Integration should check:
- That rollback cannot erase a guard accumulated across genuine crash attempts.
- That a TOCTOU between the loaded check and kickstart cannot be exploited by an operator to reset crash-loop counting and defeat rollback gating.
- That guard file writes keep owner-only permissions and atomicity.

The docs make no change to attestation, encryption, authorization (TB-011, TB-002) or billing. No security regression is evident in the docs themselves.
